newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds firm, high-yields forge gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds firm, high-yields forge gains.

text.p: U.S. corporate high-grade bonds endured a quiet session on Monday and yield spreads were mostly unchanged as the Treasury market resumed its rebound from lows seen Friday morning, traders said.
High-yield debt recovered marginal losses of Friday, meanwhile, traders said. The market was otherwised focused on the $2.15 billion in expected issuance this week.

Back in investment grades, followthrough buying from lows of last week resumed on Monday, although traders said the activity paled to that seen on Friday when investors seized the buying opportunities presented by stock and bond losses.

"We've seen better buying for the long end of the market," one trader said. "When the market sold off on Friday it hit some yield bogeys for clients and they bought high-grade corporates and a fair amount of paper left the Street."

Some of last week's darlings were quiet on Monday, however, including cable giant TCI Communications Inc. Traders said a New York Times article highlighting the company's recent revenue crunch sapped some of the better sentiments nurtured over the past week, and spreads were flat.
Elsewhere, year-end selling was judged minimal, if any, by a host of traders and analysts.
Some big high-grades issues set to come this week include:

-Deutsche Bank with a $1.0 billion offering of 10-year yankee debt via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell; Crown Cork & Seal Inc with a $1.2 billion debt offering via Salomon Brothers Inc; and Nike Inc with a $150 million seven-year debt offering via Goldman Sachs & Co.

Turning to the high-yield sector, dealers said prices eked out 1/4 point gains on light volume. While the market was predominantly focused on the more than $2 billion of new issues set to come this week, dealers also pointed to a mild recussitation of bids for some wireless cables.

CAI Wireless Systems Inc, hit hardest on Friday, still drifted lower on Monday and was quoted at 50 bid, 55 offer late in the session. The debt dropped by more than 20 points on Friday after news the Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp may reevaluate the method they use in getting video to homes. The regional Bells have $100 million invested in CAI.

People's Choice TV and American Telecasting debt was steady to higher, meanwhile. Peoples Choice debt traded up two points to 34 bid, 36 offer after losing about 10 points on Friday and Atel zeros of 2005 were little changed at 39 bid, 45 offer.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closed up 20/32 to yield 6.46 percent.
